scope: identity-gated AWS solve-worker registration and dispatch CLI, task configuration, and images

tests.command: uv run pytest tests/test_sandbox.py tests/test_worker_runtime.py tests/test_operations_deployment.py -q
assertions: AWS worker commands require explicit setup or dispatch opt-in before client construction
worker manifest checks compare the live STS principal to the startup-guard identity and role
registration serializes capacity changes and refuses to exceed the environment manifest cap
registration creates a bounded, idempotent solve worker with a verified worker-config artifact
Terraform object-store endpoint and bucket injection is reconciled against the environment manifest
solve-worker guest SSH identity references are role-scoped, temporary and removed after use

static_checks.terraform_staging_init_validate: passed with Terraform 1.13.5 and AWS provider 6.36.0
static_checks.terraform_production_init_validate: passed with Terraform 1.13.5 and AWS provider 6.36.0

solve_worker.smoke: pcb-worker --help and non-root OpenSSH client startup passed

infrastructure_safety.migrator_s3_access: internal worker-config and provisional artifact prefixes only

limitations: No authorized staging account, region, budget, deployed manifest, guest AMI, host-key bundle, candidate image allowlist, or spend authorization is available.
The CLI and task path were tested locally with synthetic manifests and a fake STS client; no live AWS registration or dispatch was attempted.
Evaluation, judging, scoring and publication processors remain separate implementation work.
